title: Officer who fired fatal shot off duty; Two members of Amherstburg police force off on stress leave, chief confirms
article: One of the Amherstburg police officers involved in the fatal shooting of Robert Scott Carpenter was off-duty when the incident occurred, The Windsor Star has learned.
The officer, who was not one who fired the fatal shot, had finished his shift and was on his way home when he responded to a colleagues' call for backup, said a source within the justice system.
Amherstburg Police Chief Brian Bird said he couldn't comment on the incident as the province's police watchdog continues to probe the Oct. 30 shooting.
He confirmed the officers involved in the incident are off on stress leave and said the tragedy has exacted a toll on the town's tight-knit police force.
"These types of situations are most difficult and the service is coping the best we can," said Bird.
The Special Investigations Unit, the civilian agency investigating the shooting, has designated one Amherstburg policeman as the "subject" officer and three others as "witness" officers.
Jon Ansell of the SIU wouldn't comment whether one of the officers was off-duty. He said the SIU hoped to release their findings early next week.
The officers involved have not been named and will only be named if charges are laid.
Bird said he, as police chief, was required by law to initiate an investigation into the incident and report to the town's police services board.
Sources say the OPP will assist in conducting a parallel investigation once the SIU has wrapped up the probe.
Bird said he hadn't contacted the OPP to seek their assistance but that he hadn't ruled it out.
"We'll cross that bridge when we get to it," he said.
Carpenter, 41, bled to death after being shot in the femoral artery by an unidentified Amherstburg police officer.
Police had arrived at his 238 McCurdy Dr. home shortly after 7 a.m. in response to a 911 call.
Police sources said officers were summoned to a domestic situation and that Carpenter lunged at one police officer with a knife and was shot by another.
Carpenter lived in the home with his common-law-wife Lisa Stewart and their two children -- three-year-old Sarah and two-year-old Noah.
They were all home at the time of the shooting.
